children: Gold prices are headed for a weekly loss of more than 2%, weighed down by surging oil prices, higher bond yields and rising rate-hike expectations. In midmorning European trading, New York gold futures fall 0.5% to $4,383.90 a troy ounce. U.S. producer prices rose in August, reinforcing concerns that surging energy costs due to Middle East disruptions are feeding back into inflation. All eyes are now on the CPI release due later on Friday. According to the CME Group's FedWatch tool, traders are now pricing in a 67% chance that the Federal Reserve will hike interest rates next week. (giulia.petroni@wsj.com)
